newsitem.title: INDIA: Tax planning helps India Reliance up profit - Daewoo.
newsitem.headline: Tax planning helps India Reliance up profit - Daewoo.

text.p: Tax planning helped India's Reliance Industries pay lower taxes and thereby raise post-tax profit for the year ended March 31, 1997, Daewoo Securities said in a research report on Wednesday.

After a board meeting on Tuesday, Reliance, India's largest private firm, said it's net profit for the year was 13.23 billion rupees. That was well a consensus forecast of 12.06 billion rupees given by a Reuter survey of 28 analysts.
"One interesting feature of FY97 result which has left analysts bewildered is the provision for tax," Daewoo Securities analyst Sonal Jain said in an analysis on the firm's results.
Analysts said they expected Reliance to explain the lower tax outgo at an analysts meeting on Wednesday evening.

For 1996/97, a company whose taxable income is less than 30 percent of pre-tax book profit will have to pay a minimum alternate tax (MAT) on 30 percent of pre-tax book profit, which amounts to 12.9 percent on the pre-tax book profit, Daewoo said.

"As per Reliance's FY97 results, the company's profit before tax (PBT) is 13,680 million rupees. This should result in a MAT of 13,680 rupees multiplied by 12.9 percent, that is 1,765 million rupees."

However, the company provided for MAT of just 450 million rupees. "However, reading between the lines, we feel we have been able to pinpoint the ingenious tax planning used by Reliance to pay lower taxes," Jain said in her report.
"Reliance has changed the method of calculating depreciation for certain assets from straight line method (SLM) to written down value (WDV) method," the report said.
Under the Companies Act, the rate of depreciation on SLM method is lower than WDV method (5.28 percent against 15.33 percent for coninuous plant and machinery).

"This entails a higher depreciation under WDV method in the earlier years," Daewoo Securities said. "Over the life of the asset it will converge towards the depreciation under SLM eventually falling below it."

The figures by Reliance show the changed method of depreciation has resulted in the current year's profit being understated by a mere 660 million rupees, which indicates that the depreciation method has been changed for relatively older assets, the report said.

"However, the cumulative depreciation over past years has increased by 9,420 million rupees. This difference has been adjusted by reducing the general reserves directly, without passing through the profit and loss account," it said.

"By deploying this method, Reliance has managed to arrive at two sets of PBT figures. The first one being the declared one and the second one in which the prior period difference in depreciation will be routed through profit and loss account and used for calculating MAT," the report said.
"Over the next few years, the profit under WDV (for assets where depreciation policy has changed) will increase as the depreciation provision under WDV will be lower," it said.
